Launched at some point between [[21 BBY]] and [[19 BBY]] during the [[Clone Wars]], the massive '''invasion of Saleucami''' was undertaken by the [[Confederacy of Independent Systems]] on the [[Outer Rim Territories|Outer Rim]] [[planet]] [[Saleucami]]. The planet had previously been the site of a [[Battle of Saleucami|battle]] between the Confederacy and [[Galactic Republic]] in 21 [['ABY-BBY' dating system|BBY]], but the Confederacy returned to Saleucami with a massive [[Confederacy military|military]] force after realizing the world could be useful as an outpost, staging area, and trans-shipment point for the [[Salin Corridor]] [[hyperspace route]]. Toward the end of the Clone Wars, the Republic initiated the [[Siege of Saleucami]] as part of the [[Outer Rim Sieges]] to claim Saleucami from its enemy faction.

==Prelude==
{{Quote|So… I see the war has finally made its way out here…|[[Farmer]] [[Cut Lawquane]] notes that the Clone Wars have come to Saleucami|<ref name="The Deserter">{{TCW|The Deserter}}</ref>}}
[[File:Saleucami-TD.png|thumb|right|250px|Saleucami's peaceful existence ended when it became a major site of the Clone Wars.]]
Despite being a quiet, backwater [[planet]] in the [[Outer Rim Territories]]<ref name="Battles that Changed the Galaxy">''[[Star Wars: Battles that Changed the Galaxy]]''</ref> without much strategic value, in part due to its lack of natural resources,<ref name="Mustafar citation 2">{{EncyclopediaCite|Mustafar and Other Planets in the Outer Rim}} {{C|French edition}} {{C|Original text in French: "Saleucami était un monde isolé sans aucune valeur particulière. La Guerre des Clones arriva pourtant jusqu'à lui." and "Située dans le secteur Suolriep du système du même nom, Saleucami était un monde peu peuplé, sans ressources naturelles suffisantes pour une exploitation industrielle à grande échelle."}}</ref> the world of [[Saleucami]] came to be of [[Triad of Evil|great importance]] in the [[Clone Wars]] between the [[Confederacy of Independent Systems]] and the [[Galactic Republic]],<ref name="Battles that Changed the Galaxy">''[[Star Wars: Battles that Changed the Galaxy]]''</ref> even though the small community<ref name="Scarif and Other Planets">{{EncyclopediaCite|Scarif and Other Planets in the Outer Rim}} {{C|English edition}}</ref> of settlers on Saleucami wanted to avoid the conflict.<ref name="Saleucami databank">{{Databank|saleucami|Saleucami}}</ref> In fact, those who moved to the isolated planet often wanted to avoid the attention of the Confederacy<ref name="Mustafar citation 3">{{EncyclopediaCite|Mustafar and Other Planets in the Outer Rim}} {{C|French edition}} {{C|Original text in French: "Les colons qui migraient sur Saleucami cherchaient généralement à mener une vie paisible, souvent loin du regard des Séparatistes; c'était le cas de Cut Lawquane."}}</ref> or the Republic.<ref name="The Deserter" /> Although it would remain untouched through most of the war,<ref name="Saleucami databank" /> the Separatist [[General]] [[Grievous]] sought to take over the world<ref name="Grievous Intrigue">{{TCW|Grievous Intrigue}}</ref> in [[21 BBY]],<ref name="Date note" /> beginning a [[Battle of Saleucami|battle]] between [[Republic Military|Republic]] and [[Confederacy military|Separatist forces]] above<ref name="Grievous Intrigue" /> and on the surface of the planet.<ref name="The Deserter" />

Although [[Jedi Master]] [[Eeth Koth]] was rescued from Grievous's custody,<ref name="Grievous Intrigue" /> the [[cyborg]] general [[Gender|himself]] managed to escape after a chase on the world.<ref name="The Deserter" /> Following the event, it seemed as though Saleucami would return to its peaceful status, but [[Separatist officer]]s had other plans;<ref name="Battles that Changed the Galaxy" /> Grievous's journey on Saleucami had convinced him that the planet would be decent,<ref name="Scarif and Other Planets" /> but successful, as an outpost<ref name="Mustafar and Other Outer Rim Planets" /> and staging area.<ref name="Scarif and Other Planets" /> Indeed, as the [[Perlemian Trade Route]] grew increasingly contested, Separatist [[convoy]]s needed a safer [[hyperspace route]] for travel. As Saleucami happened to be close to the regional [[Salin Corridor]], Separatist [[Commanding officer|commanders]] realized Saleucami could be useful as a stockpile for materiel produced in the [[Foundry of the Confederacy]], a grouping of [[factory world]]s in the [[Mid Rim Territories|Mid]] and Outer Rims.<ref name="Battles that Changed the Galaxy" /> Between 21 [['ABY-BBY' dating system|BBY]] and [[20 BBY]],<ref name="Kenobi battle date">[[Obi-Wan 4|''Obi-Wan'' 4]] establishes that the battle of [[Saleucami]] it features in flashbacks was fought between the [[Battle of Ryloth]], which ended in "[[Liberty on Ryloth]]," and the [[Devaron massacre]], which occurred in "[[Monster]]." Per the reasoning [[Template:TCWcanondates|here]], the events of "Liberty on Ryloth" can be dated to [[21 BBY]], while the events of "Monster" can be dated to [[20 BBY]]. As such, that battle of Saleucami must occur between those two [[Standard year|years]].</ref> the Republic was involved in another [[Battle of Saleucami (Mekedrix)|battle on Saleucami]].<ref name="Obi-Wan 4">[[Obi-Wan 4|''Obi-Wan'' 4]]</ref>

==The invasion==
After realizing the planet's usefulness as a potential trans-shipment point,<ref name="Battles that Changed the Galaxy" /> the Confederacy launched a massive invasion of Saleucami<ref name="TCW encyclopedia" /> with a large [[Saleucami force|military force]] under the [[Commanding officer|command]] of Grievous<ref name="Mustafar and Other Outer Rim Planets" /> at some point between 21 BBY and [[19 BBY]].<ref name="Date note" /> As the Separatist force was large enough to confront a [[fleet]] of [[starship]]s [[Blockade|blockading]] the planet and landed on Saleucami,<ref name="Mustafar and Other Outer Rim Planets" /> the invasion of Saleucami<ref name="Catalyst" /> brought widespread fighting to the planet.<ref name="Collapse" />

==Aftermath==
{{Quote|Saleucami has fallen, and Master Vos has moved his troops to Boz Pity.|[[Jedi General]] [[Obi-Wan Kenobi]] reports that the Republic has liberated Saleucami|<ref name="Date note" />}}
[[File:BARCspeeder_DB.png|thumb|left|250px|The once-peaceful planet of Saleucami became a center of fighting after the Separatist invasion.]]
Escalating the fighting for Saleucami, the invasion brought the Clone Wars back to the planet,<ref name="TCW encyclopedia" /> where the Confederacy would station its large force with the support of a blockade fleet.<ref name="Scarif and Other Planets" /> [[Dressellian]] [[smuggler]] [[Has Obitt]], whose missions with [[Lieutenant Commander]] [[Orson Callan Krennic|Orson Krennic]] of the [[Republic Special Weapons Group]] had left him unwelcome in Separatist territory, narrowly missed the invasion, but he later found himself amid the [[sneak attack on Roche]].<ref name="Catalyst" /> Sometime after the Separatists took control of Saleucami and made it into a factory world, the Republic, fearing the secrets the Separatist-controlled world held, [[Siege of Saleucami|besieged]] the world in the final [[Standard month|months]] of the Clone Wars<ref name="Battles that Changed the Galaxy" /> during the [[Outer Rim Sieges]] campaign.<ref name="DB Neyo">{{Databank|clone-commander-neyo|Clone Commander Neyo}}</ref> Like the Separatist invasion before it, the Republic siege brought widespread conflict to the world.<ref name="Collapse" /> Following the war, the [[Galactic Empire]],<ref name="Cut Lawquane">{{Databank|cut-lawquane|Cut Lawquane}}</ref> successor state of the Republic,<ref name="Catalyst" /> remained interested in Saleucami<ref name="Cut Lawquane" /> and attempted to bring Imperial order to the previously peaceful planet.<ref name="Saleucami databank" />

==Behind the scenes==
The invasion of Saleucami was first mentioned in [[James Luceno]]'s [[2016]] novel, ''[[Catalyst: A Rogue One Novel]]''.<ref name="Catalyst" /> The invasion was further expanded upon in the French release of the booklet "[[Mustafar and Other Planets in the Outer Rim]],"<ref name="Mustafar and Other Outer Rim Planets" /> which was released in France on [[April 8]], [[2022]]<ref name="Altaya">{{Altaya|lang=fr|url=livres-bd/encyclopedie-star-wars|text=Official Star Wars Encyclopedia}}</ref> as part of [[De Agostini]]'s [[Star Wars Encyclopedia (series)|''Star Wars Encyclopedia'']] line.<ref name="Mustafar and Other Outer Rim Planets" /> However, when the booklet was released in English in [[2023]], the section on Saleucami was removed.<ref name="Mustafar English">{{EncyclopediaCite|Mustafar and Other Planets in the Outer Rim}} {{C|English edition}}</ref> It had been moved to the booklet "[[Scarif and Other Planets in the Outer Rim]]," which released in 2022.<ref name="Scarif and Other Planets" /> Instead, the English Mustafar encyclopedia contains two pages on the [[Fortress Inquisitorius]].<ref name="Mustafar English" /> Additionally, mentions of the invasion of Saleucami<ref name="Mustafar and Other Outer Rim Planets" /> were removed from and altered in the English release of the Saleucami passage.<ref name="Scarif and Other Planets" /> This article assumes both language releases can be taken as [[canon]], but cites information found only in one release to that specific language version.
